title: XIV: Hester and the Physician

teacherSummary.text: On the shore Hester confronts Chillingworth, who has grown darker and fiendish. She asks him to stop tormenting the minister and says she will reveal his identity. He admits he has become a fiend but says he cannot pardon; it is all 'a dark necessity'.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “I have left thee to the scarlet letter” slowly and put it in my own words: Refusing to plead with Chillingworth, Hester tells him she leaves him to the scarlet letter. Next, craft. I notice she speaks of the letter as if it were a judge who will deal with him, the way people say "I leave you to God." The strongest word is “letter”: the symbol of her own punishment becomes, in her words, the power that will judge him too. Then, effect. Why does Hester leave Chillingworth "to the scarlet letter"? My answer: Hester means that the letter's lesson, the cost of hidden sin, applies to him; his secret revenge has made him guiltier than she is, and she will no longer beg him for mercy.

Theme link: revenge has made a wise man into a fiend. Credit any position that is supported by quotation and reasoning; push one-sided answers to address the strongest counterpoint.

middleSchool.note: Excerpt-based: read the passage aloud first; use the scaffolds; accept partial answers and build with probes.

hsFreshman.note: Use the scaffolds for literal and inferential items; require one quotation for every inferential answer.

hsSophomore.note: Require a quotation and an explanation; push evaluative answers to address a counterclaim.

hsJunior.note: Emphasize structure and ambiguity; students should name where the text leaves matters open.

hsSenior.note: Weigh competing interpretations; students should defend the stronger reading.

ap.note: Treat each evaluative item as a thesis rehearsal: defensible claim, purposeful evidence, commentary on choices.

collegeFreshman.note: Add the extension: connect answers to historical context and one secondary perspective.

collegeSophomore.note: Use the extensions: genre and period conventions, and a published critic.

collegeJunior.note: Use the extensions: name a critical method and test it against the passage.

collegeSenior.note: Use the extensions: connect the chapter to the whole work and the scholarship.

graduate.note: Use the extensions: position answers in a critical conversation and the textual history.
